title: RUSVEL is the estate's ports-and-adapters coordination layer over capability-tenant-infra, skill-eco, and autobiz-kit — narrow in what it executes, broad in where it reaches, proven first on mbaneshi.ir
rationale: Supersedes strategy-rusvel-scope-vs-anthropic-native, whose framing (narrow RUSVEL to a deterministic core exposed via MCP) was correct on 'don't rebuild orchestration' but incomplete: it treated RUSVEL as one more capability rather than the coordination layer sitting above capability-tenant-infra (CTI, self-hosted Windmill/Directus/Supabase, tenant x capability model, live behind houshkar.ir and parvandeh). A single 2026-09-03 session (spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-rusvel-as-estate-abstraction.md) established that the same 'AI runs departments, human at the gate' idea had already been independently rebuilt at least four times (CTI, zix-agent vs Hermes/Managed Agents, RUSVEL itself, two shared operating manuals), and that CTI, skill-eco, autobiz-kit and ~/infra already cover tenant-scoped execution, skill curation, per-client delivery, and an MCP/CLI harness respectively -- none of which RUSVEL should reimplement. RUSVEL's own founding philosophy (docs/design/vision.md: ports and adapters, swap Claude for Ollama, swap SQLite for Supabase) already matches the shape needed: narrow in what it executes (no agent-loop, no tenant-execution, no skill-curation rebuild), broad in where it reaches (every venture, every capability, every model, via ports). The one real gap is that dept-*/DepartmentApp assumes tenant = self; adding a tenant axis is what turns 'multiple roles tailored to each initiative' from aspiration into fact. Decision: RUSVEL is the estate's ports-and-adapters coordination layer -- CTI's hands, skill-eco's curated skills, and autobiz-kit's per-client islands are adapters RUSVEL wires to, not rivals. Proven bottom-up on one real venture (mbaneshi.ir: content pipeline first, outreach/leads second) before any part of this is generalized to other tenants -- per the estate's own repeatedly-relearned lesson against building infrastructure ahead of proven need. User confirmed this framing explicitly across several turns ('those capability, do not fight with rusvel, they are complete each other') and requested this refinement locked once the spec existed.

title: Continue building RUSVEL in Rust; do not start a parallel Bun+Postgres rewrite
rationale: Three docs committed 2026-04-01 (empowered-claude-code.md, new-system-design-brief.md, vision-v3.md) proposed a fresh repo on Bun + PostgreSQL + pgvector, with a Claude Code memory MCP server as phase 1. But 27 GitHub issues filed 2026-08-25 (5 months later) all invest in the existing Rust codebase, including issue #13 'MCP-first: expose all 13 department toolsets via rusvel --mcp' — which covers the same phase-1 goal (persistent memory + department context surfaced to Claude Code via MCP). The Rust side already has the MCP server, FTS5 session memory, and ScopedToolRegistry needed for that goal. No evidence of the Bun rewrite being started was found in sibling repos or the fa digest archive (search recall was degraded - vector index was down). Under financial pressure, restarting in a new stack throws away 5 months of August work for a goal already ~80% covered by open issue #13. User confirmed agreement in-session: 'i am with you'.

title: Scope RUSVEL around vendor-independent core + MCP integration surface, not generic agent-orchestration parity with Anthropic's native tooling
rationale: Anthropic ships agent orchestration daily (Cowork scheduled tasks, Claude Code subagents/hooks/Routines, connectors, cross-surface memory) — see the Sept 2026 'Solo Unicorn Operating Manual' which runs a 10-desk solo-company pattern entirely on Claude's native surfaces with no custom software. Competing feature-for-feature on generic agent-loop/chat-UX parity is an unwinnable race against a vendor shipping that layer for free as part of a subscription the user already pays for. RUSVEL's defensible value sits elsewhere: (1) vendor independence via rusvel-llm's swappable ports (Claude API/CLI, OpenAI, Ollama) — the manual's own Reality-checks section names single-vendor-account dependency as a company-ending risk, which RUSVEL's ports-and-adapters architecture directly solves; (2) a deterministic, auditable domain core (finance ledger, legal compliance register, job-queue approval gate, harvest scorer) that wants correctness guarantees rather than AI-native behavior; (3) local-first zero-ops operation (SQLite + Ollama, no cloud dependency); (4) MCP as the integration seam (issue #13 exposed 94 tools over rusvel --mcp) letting Claude Code / Cowork / Claude.ai drive RUSVEL as hands-and-record-keeping, instead of RUSVEL reimplementing their agent loop. Decision: continue building RUSVEL (reaffirms strategy-continue-rust-not-bun-rewrite), but reallocate marginal effort away from generic orchestration/chat-UX parity toward engine domain-logic correctness and the MCP surface. User raised the viability question directly ('doses our app still worth pursue') and confirmed this framing in-session.
